title: Title
notes: Open by describing the appendix as more than a glossary. Each symbol is treated as a small contract: it names an object, declares a sample space, states the transformations that are allowed, and points to computations elsewhere in the course.

title: Type Check
notes: Use this slide to give students a repeatable lookup habit. A symbol should not be interpreted by memory alone; it should be read through object type, support, invariance, and course use before any formula is trusted.

title: Space Gallery
notes: The gallery is the visual anchor for the appendix. Stress that the coordinate array is secondary: the first question is which constraint the observation must satisfy and which transformations leave the object unchanged. Have learners say out loud whether rotations, sign flips, or basis changes are supposed to be invisible before naming a statistic.

title: Space Table
notes: Treat this as a safety table rather than a vocabulary table. The important teaching move is to pair every sample-space symbol with a common invalid shortcut that would silently leave the geometry of the problem.

title: Quantities
notes: Pause here to separate estimands from estimates. Directional statistics reuses familiar letters, so students need to know whether a symbol belongs to the model, the observed sample, or an estimating equation before interpreting it. Then ask what evidence would change the population claim and what object would carry that evidence.

title: Resultant
notes: The resultant slide makes a familiar formula visual. Emphasize that the direction and length are two different pieces of evidence: direction tells where the vector points, while length tells whether that direction is persuasive. This prevents interpreting a short resultant as a precise direction and helps distinguish lack of direction from second-moment structure.

title: Family Routing
notes: Explain that a model name is not a decorative label. It asserts a support, a parameterization, and a diagnostic route; choosing the wrong family usually means the wrong invariance has already been assumed. A model that lives on the wrong support is not approximately right in the glossary sense; it is answering a different geometric question.

title: Special Functions
notes: Keep the discussion concrete: special-function symbols should not intimidate students as isolated analysis. In this course they are calculator names for normalization, inversion, and moment matching in directional models. When a function appears, learners should annotate the equation with its role before manipulating it algebraically.

title: Axial Data
notes: Use axial data to show how notation enforces invariance. The sign of an axis is arbitrary, so a first-moment arrow can be misleading, while the scatter matrix keeps the information that survives sign reversal. The goal is for students to swap from vector summaries to quadratic summaries whenever the observation is projective.

title: Matrix Manifolds
notes: This slide connects notation with executable checks. Matrix-manifold symbols should make students ask whether orthogonality, determinant, and projection identities have been preserved by the calculation. The right response is to reproject or flag the computation, not to keep using a convenient but invalid matrix.

title: Shape Symbols
notes: Shape notation is a compact reminder that the data have been quotienting away nuisance transformations. The instructor should emphasize that the same landmarks before centering and scaling do not yet live in shape space. This prevents a slide about shape from quietly turning back into ordinary multivariate coordinates.

title: Dependency Map
notes: The dependency map turns the appendix into a course index. Ask students to follow one path from a sample space to a statistic or family, because that path explains why the notation matters in later calculations.

title: Executable Atlas
notes: Connect the lecture deck back to the notebook without listing files. The central point is that structured records make notation reusable: later notebooks can inspect the same supports, invariants, and diagnostics instead of redefining symbols casually.

title: Pitfalls
notes: Use the pitfalls as a quality-control checklist for the rest of the course. Each failure begins with a symbol being read without its support or invariant, and each fix is to restore the missing geometric contract.

title: Recap
notes: Close by returning to the type-check habit. The prompt is deliberately about a case where first-moment notation is weak but scatter notation is informative, so learners must choose the symbol family before choosing the conclusion.
